column1: # Courtois MinRank challenges A-F.
# THESE ARE PARAMETER SETS, NOT INSTANCES. No challenge matrices were ever
# published; see docs/research/minrank.md section 3 for the evidence. Anything
# built from these rows is a same-parameter surrogate, never the challenge.
# Source: N. Courtois, "Efficient Zero-knowledge Authentication Based on a
# Linear Algebra Problem MinRank", Asiacrypt 2001, LNCS 2248, pp. 402-421;
# IACR ePrint 2001/058, section 4.3 "Practical Parameter Choices", the table
# headed "Cryptosystem / Parameter set" on page 7.
# eprint.iacr.org serves 403 to this machine; the bytes read were the Wayback
# Machine's 2004-07-23 capture of the author's own ePrint PDF:
#   https://web.archive.org/web/20040723070613id_/http://eprint.iacr.org/2001/058.pdf
#   sha256 bbdfe4521eb102eb7dc137bea245f2a6ec186ee9fddf2b5b906a2cbfc0daee34
#   256966 bytes, 19 pages (accessed 2026-11-07)
# The table was additionally read as a rendered image of page 7, because
# pdftotext flattens the superscripts that carry every attack exponent.
# Confirmed against a second primary document (#382). Courtois's PhD thesis,
# "La securite des primitives cryptographiques basees sur des problemes
# algebriques multivariables : MQ, IP, MinRank, HFE", Universite Paris 6,
# 2001, Table 24.7.1 on page 183, reproduces the Asiacrypt table cell for cell
# across all eight columns and all twelve rows, including its bolding.
#   http://www.minrank.org/phd.pdf
#   1490144 bytes, 221 pages (accessed 2026-11-07), also read as a rendered
#   page image for the same superscript reason.
# Problem (section 3), verbatim in substance: given eta x n matrices
# M_0; M_1, ..., M_m over GF(q), find alpha in GF(q)^m with
#     Rank(sum_{i=1..m} alpha_i M_i - M_0) <= r.
# The formulation is INHOMOGENEOUS: the public data is 1 + m matrices, not m,
# and a verifier must subtract M_0.
# Columns
#   id            challenge letter as printed
#   q             field order; GF(65521) or GF(2)
#   eta, n        matrix shape (eta rows, n columns); eta == n for all of A-F
#   m             number of matrices M_1..M_m, i.e. the number of unknowns.
#                 The public key carries m + 1 matrices, counting M_0.
#   r             target rank, the problem asks for Rank <= r
#   pr_solution   "Pr_alpha[Rank <= r]" column, verbatim as printed
#   comm_kb_20x   "20 x Comm. [Kb]" column, verbatim as printed
#   bf kernel bigm syndrome submatrices mq
#                 base-2 logarithms of the six attack-cost rows, in the paper's
#                 order: Brute force, Kernel, Big m, Syndrome, Sub-matrices,
#                 MQ. "inf" is the paper's own infinity sign. Kernel is bolded
#                 in the source as the best attack on every one of A-F.
# These attack rows are TRANSCRIBED, not re-derived. See minrank.md section 6.3
# for the one row (D, brute force) that does not follow the rule the other five
# obey.
